# `set_user_location`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Store the user's site location (lon, lat) and push it to the mount when possible.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build registration only); stored-site change also OBSERVED 2026-10-12 |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0x7e660 (64-bit build), SaveUserLocation @0x141af0, GetCalibLocatOffset, ScopeAM5::SetSiteLatLong, registration @0x74548 (32-bit build); wire observation 2026-10-12 |

Registered in both guider dispatcher tables; the name is not in the imager tables, so a request on the main control port (4700) is not found locally (103) and reaches this handler through the imager's method-not-found relay to the guider; guest-table clients cannot use that relay. The app sends it on every connect (after pi_set_time) and when the user selects a location. READ (64-bit build): the handler parses lon and lat as numbers (104 if either is missing or not numeric), then stores them through the user-location save routine, which validates the range, writes the user longitude/latitude settings, refreshes the geographic caches and the configuration timestamp. The store outcome is only logged; the handler continues either way. Unless the imager reports the View function as running, it then calls the mount location update helper (which can query the imager for its location and set the mount site); the flag passed to that helper comes from the mount type, not from the request's force member, which is never read. Depending on the helper's outcome the reply is result 0 or an error carrying the helper's recorded code. No time-zone or host-clock change is made on this path. OBSERVED 2026-10-12 (iOS app traffic and a device run): object params with numeric lon/lat and boolean force, reply code 0 with an integer result, and the changed site was confirmed by the location_lon_lat readback of get_device_state. Precision, units and the value of force were not established by the observation. lon and lat are decimal degrees, longitude positive east (INFERRED, strong: the stored value feeds an east-positive astronomy routine and is negated for the mount's west-positive site command). The 32-bit build handler was not analysed; only its registration is READ.

Side effects: Persists the user longitude/latitude settings and refreshes the geographic caches and configuration timestamp (SaveUserLocation); unless View is running, attempts to update the mount's site location. The store happens before the mount update, so it is not undone when the mount step fails (INFERRED from call order). The stored-site change was OBSERVED 2026-10-12 via get_device_state readback.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_user_location"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | yes | - | Object with lon, lat and force, or the positional array [lon, lat, force] (longitude first, unlike scope_set_location). lon and lat are required numbers; integer or real accepted through the shared number helper. force is mapped by name but never looked up or used by the handler. The store step validates coordinate ranges (its exact thresholds are not separately established; the loader used by get_user_location accepts longitude strictly inside -360.1..360.1 and latitude inside -90.1..90.1). A failed store is logged and the handler continues, so an out-of-range pair is not by itself an error reply. The app always sends the object form with all three members (OBSERVED 2026-10-12, both force values seen). Range: at least 2 item(s). [READ; object form also OBSERVED 2026-10-12] |
| `params.lon` | number | yes | - | Site longitude in decimal degrees, positive east (INFERRED, strong; the stored value is passed unchanged to an east-positive astronomy routine and negated for the mount's west-positive site command). [READ (member and numeric parse); unit and east-positive sign INFERRED] |
| `params.lat` | number | yes | - | Site latitude, degrees INFERRED. [READ (member and numeric parse); unit INFERRED] |
| `params.force` | boolean | no | - | Sent by the app (OBSERVED, both true and false). Not read by the 64-bit handler; in particular it does not force a time or zone change, and it is not the flag passed to the mount location update. Clients MAY omit it. [READ (not used by handler); OBSERVED on the wire 2026-10-12] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | lon or lat missing or not a number | `expected int param` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

The 104 label is the shared table text, although the parse is numeric. A failed mount location update forwards the code recorded by the native mount layer; those codes are not exhausted by this table. Failure and validation behaviour was not exercised on a device.

## Example

Request, positional - Positional form (values invented); the app sends the equivalent object form with lon, lat and force:

```json
{"id":31,"method":"set_user_location","params":[10.0,50.0,false]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_user_location","result":0,"code":0,"id":31}
```
